## Claims

### C-R3-01 | 2 Sam 7 turning point; messianic promise; Abraham → David trajectory
- **Claim (attributed Tsumura):** Second Samuel 7 “announces the messianic promise” and is “a turning point in the history of salvation in the Bible.” Gen. 12:1-3 promised Abraham a great nation and blessing of nations through offspring (22:18); that promise is “confirmed and made specific” by the promise that David’s offspring will sit enthroned eternally (2 Sam. 7:12-16). The Lord makes one family, David’s, representative of his people forever; nothing suggests David deserved this favor — it is according to God’s own heart (v. 21) that he promises David’s descendants his grace / steadfast love ḥesed (v. 15).
- **Quote:** "Second Samuel 7, which announces the messianic promise, is a turning point in the history of salvation in the Bible."
- **Locus:** §E intro; 2 Sam 7; slice L1–5 / raw ~4151–4155
- **Targets:** [[2-samuel]], [[davidic-covenant]], [[david]], [[david-tsumura]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R3-02 | “Davidic covenant” label; berît absent in 7:8-17 but present in Ps 89
- **Claim:** Verses 8-17 are often described as the “Davidic covenant,” though the term “covenant” does not appear there. Ps. 89:3 describes this promise: “I have made a covenant with my chosen one.” berît appears several times in Ps 89 (vv. 3, 28, 34); key word-pairs from ch. 7 also appear: ḥesed – ʾĕmûnāh; zeraʿ – kissēʾ; ḥesed – covenant.
- **Quote:** "Verses 8-17 are often described as the “Davidic covenant,” even though the term “covenant” does not appear there. But in Ps. 89:3 this promise is described using the words, “I have made a covenant with my chosen one.”"
- **Locus:** §E intro; Ps 89:1-4, 19-35 cited; slice L6–79 / raw ~4156–4229
- **Targets:** [[davidic-covenant]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R3-03 | Ps 89:36-37 AXX′B quadracolon; heir as “faithful witness”; Christian messianic reading
- **Claim:** Ps 89:36-37 should be treated as a quadracolon (AXX′B): middle parallel lines X//X′ inserted between A and B, which hold a vertical grammatical relationship — “His heir shall be forever as the faithful witness on the clouds.” This David’s heir will be the “faithful witness” on the clouds. According to “Christian canonical understanding,” this heir of David is the Messiah to come (Rev. 3:14; 1:5).
- **Quote:** "According to the Christian canonical understanding, this heir of David is the Messiah to come (see Rev. 3:14; 1:5)."

### C-R3-04 | Covenant “forever”; eternal covenant concept not late (Hittite parallel)
- **Claim:** The covenant was to be “forever” (2 Sam. 7:16; Ps. 89:36). berît ʿôlām appears sixteen times in the Bible (e.g. Isa 24:5; 55:3; Jer 32:40; Ezek 37:26), including the “Last Words of David” (2 Sam. 23:5). The concept is not late — illustrated by Hittite “eternal treaty” in the second millennium B.C.
- **Quote:** "the concept is not a late one, as illustrated by the Hittite use of the expression “eternal treaty” during the second millennium B.C."
- **Locus:** §E intro; slice L100–101 / raw ~4250–4251
- **Targets:** [[davidic-covenant]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R3-05 | One-sided grant like Abraham, not Sinai bilateral obligations
- **Claim:** The “covenant” in 2 Sam. 7 did not specify obligations of two parties like the Sinai covenant (Exod. 20-31), but was “a one-sided promise, a grant or promise” like the one to Abraham (Gen. 12:1-3; 15:18-21; 17:1-21). David desires to build a house for the Lord; the Lord does not approve and on his own initiative will establish David’s house (dynasty) eternally, promising an eternal throne (v. 16).
- **Quote:** "the “covenant” in 2 Sam. 7 did not specify the obligations of two parties like the Sinai covenant in Exod. 20-31, but was a one-sided promise, a grant or promise like the one to Abraham"
- **Locus:** §E intro; 2 Sam 7:16; slice L103–105 / raw ~4253–4255
- **Targets:** [[davidic-covenant]], [[david]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R3-06 | Ps 132 “sure oath”; Solomon near term; Jesus eternal messianic trajectory
- **Claim:** Psalm 132 says the Lord promised David with “a sure oath” that “one of the sons of your body I will set on your throne” (v. 11; 2 Sam. 7:12). This points to Solomon who would sit on Israel’s throne and build the house for the LORD’s name (1 K. 8:20), and “eventually, to Jesus, the Messiah who will sit on the throne eternally (Luke 1:32-33).” Cross-refs: Ps 89:20-38; Isa 55:3; Jer 33:17, 20-22; 2 Chr 13:5; 21:7.
- **Quote:** "This points to Solomon who would “sit on the throne of Israel” and build “the house for the name of the LORD” (1 K. 8:20), and eventually, to Jesus, the Messiah who will sit on the throne eternally (Luke 1:32-33)."

### C-R3-07 | Literary-composition theories of ch. 7; Sergi’s three stages
- **Claim:** Scholars usually hold the entire chapter as Deuteronomistic product; recently some accept preexilic/pre-Dtr material — debate is how much. O. Sergi claims Nathan’s oracle had three stages: (I) earliest layer vv. 1a, 2-3, 11b (late 9th–early 8th c.; positive; divine legitimacy of dynasty, not temple); (II) Dtr layer vv. 1b, 4-6a, 8-9, 11a, 12-16 (late 7th c. Josiah; cultic interest; temple + dynasty; founding text of Davidic monarchy); (III) post-Dtr vv. 6b-7, 10 (Persian period; Priestly; disregards dynasty importance in building temple).
- **Quote:** "It has usually been held among scholars that the entire chapter is most likely a product of the Deuteronomistic writing."
- **Locus:** EXCURSUS: Theories of Literary Composition of 2 Samuel 7; slice L109–122 / raw ~4259–4272
- **Targets:** [[2-samuel]], [[nathan]], [[davidic-covenant]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R3-08 | Apparent “rest” tense inconsistency used for layers; Tsumura rejects discrepancy
- **Claim:** Vv. 1b and 11a both speak about “rest”; conventional BH verbal-tense view takes waYHWH hēnîaḥ-lô (v. 1b) as PAST (“the LORD had given him rest”) and wahănîḥōtî lekā (v. 11a) as FUTURE (“I will give you rest”) — creating temporal inconsistency within the supposed Dtr layer itself. Tsumura: recent work on tense/aspect and discourse grammar shows that the verbal-tense “discrepancy” used to argue for several literary layers in 2 Sam. 7 “is not actually a discrepancy.”
- **Quote:** "the discrepancy in the tense of Hebrew verbs that is used to argue for several different literary layers in 2 Sam. 7, is not actually a discrepancy."
- **Locus:** Composition excursus; slice L123–126 / raw ~4273–4276
- **Targets:** [[davidic-covenant]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R3-09 | ANE eternal kingship / dynasty background (Hammurabi, Ugarit, Assyria)
- **Claim:** Idea of eternal kingship existed among Israel’s neighbors at least since beginning of 2nd millennium B.C. (Code of Hammurabi prologue i.26: eternal kingship of Marduk “as fixed as heaven and earth”). Ugarit Baal Cycle KTU 1.2 IV 10: mlk ʿlmk “eternal kingship”; letter RS 18.113A+B prayers for “eternal kingship”; mlk ʿlm for El and deified king (KTU 1.108). Eternal kingship ≠ identical to eternal dynasty, but dynastic succession forever reasonably based on it. Laato: Assyrian royal building inscriptions express eternal dynasty from 2nd millennium; concept could play role in Israelite royal ideology at David’s time. Assyrian “eternity” may mean perpetuance/stability; in Bible also “future time” (HALOT).
- **Quote:** "the idea of eternal kingship had existed among countries neighboring Israel at least since the beginning of the second millennium B.C"
- **Locus:** EXCURSUS: 2 Samuel 7 in Its ANE Context; slice L129–152 / raw ~4279–4302
- **Targets:** [[davidic-covenant]], [[david]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R3-11 | 7:1-3 David’s desire; rest as setting; ANE temple-building in peace
- **Claim:** When the king was living in his house — the LORD had given him rest from all enemies around — he tells Nathan he lives in a house of cedars while the ark sits among curtains. Nathan: do whatever is in your mind, for the LORD is with you. Desire to build temple influenced by rest situation; ANE temple building best in peace/prosperity (Gudea Cylinders / Averbeck). David contrasts cedar house (5:11) with tent housing ark (6:17). Natural for king to build temple. Nathan’s “the LORD is with you” is general counselor comment; that night he receives specific revelation as prophet/messenger.
- **Quote:** "David’s desire to build the temple for the Lord is apparently influenced by his current situation, that the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies around."

- **Claim:** Much confusion over which parts of prophecy are past vs future. Hebrew verbs do not express tense like English. ### C-R3-21 | weqtl shift 9b-11a: majority future (NRSV) creates rest contradiction; PAST preferred
- **Claim:** Until 9a narrative qtl–wayqtl–wayqtl; at 9b sudden change to weqtl–weqtl–weqtl. Virtually all versions take as waw consecutive perfect = imperfect/future (NRSV: will make great name; will appoint place; will give rest) — leading to contradiction between v. 11a future rest and v. 1b past rest. KJV took 11a PAST; Anderson and some others PAST; Elberfelder both possibilities. McCarter/McKenzie take 11a futuristic and treat 1b as secondary marginal note. Chronicles omits rest theme in both 17:1 and 17:10a (“I will subdue”) — Tsumura: different focus (result *nwḥ vs act *knʿ), does not prove Samuel’s rest phrase secondary.
- **Quote:** "Such an interpretation, however, leads to a contradiction between v. 11a (“and I will give you rest from all your enemies”) and v. 1b (“the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies around him”)."

### C-R3-23 | Discourse-grammar analysis of oracle levels: PAST–PROCEDURAL–PRESENT–FUTURE
- **Claim (core Tsumura argument):** Prophetic speech 8b-16 has layered discourse: NARRATIVE PAST 8b-9a (qtl–wayqtl); PROCEDURAL 9b-11aα (weqtl “how-it-was-done,” Longacre); RESULT 11aβ (weqtl rest); DECLARATIVE PRESENT performative 11b (weqtl the Lord tells you); PREDICTIVE FUTURE 12-16 (yqtl–weqtl). Primary level: what-happened (took; was with; cut off). Secondary: continuous dealings (making great name; providing place; planting) → consequence rest. Then future: make a house for David. 9b-11aβ transition from past dealings to future promise. Parallel discourse patterns: 1 Sam 17:38; Jer 37:15. LXX mixed aorist/future on these verbs.
- **Quote:** "NARRATIVE (8b-9a) PAST (qtl - wayqtl) PROCEDURAL (9b-11aα) (weqtl…) RESULT (11aβ)… DECLARATIVE (11b) PRESENT performative… PREDICTIVE (12-16) FUTURE"
- **Locus:** EXCURSUS: A Discourse Grammatical Point of View; slice L397–472 / raw ~4547–4622
- **Targets:** [[davidic-covenant]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]], [[nathan]]

### C-R3-30 | Speaker-oriented ʿal-kēn in 7:22; AXX′B monotheism confession
- **Claim:** Against Alter’s suspicion of another writer for elevated style: David was a noted poet. In v. 22 ʿal-kēn is speaker-oriented (“Therefore [I say], you are great”) — God’s deeds show he is great; not “promise made him great.” Comparative negation: no one like you; no God besides you. Labuschagne: incomparability → uniqueness → monotheism (cf. Ps 86:8-10; Deut 4:34-35; 1 Sam 2:2). Grammatically read as AXX′B quadracolon: A You are great… X/X′ none like you / no God besides you… B in all that we heard with our ears — be = “in” not forced “according to.” Excursus lists speaker-oriented ʿal-kēn elsewhere (1 Sam 5:5; 19:24b; 2 Sam 5:8b; Job 9:22b; lākēn Gen 4:15).
- **Quote:** "This is an explicit statement of monotheism; compare 1 Sam. 2:2."
- **Locus:** 7:22 + EXCURSUS speaker-oriented ʿal-kēn; slice L649–768 / raw ~4799–4918
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R3-31 | 7:23-24 Israel’s incomparability; *pdh double sense; angels; covenant people forever
- **Claim:** Who like your people Israel, the only nation (gôy ʾeḥād; not “other nation”). ʾĕlōhîm with plural verb “went” better “angels/divine beings” (agents; Ps 78:49) than “God” (contra LXX/Chr “God”). Two *pdh senses: (1) pay ransom for / redeem; (2) release from — paralleled in Ugaritic legal KTU 3.4. Poetic parallel relative clauses both modify “only nation.” MT gôyīm wēlōhâw: enclitic mem → “from the nation and its gods” = Egypt only. V. 24 continues relative: established Israel as people forever while Lord became their God — reconfirms special covenant between incomparable God and incomparable people. Textual notes on lākem, mippenê ʿammekā.
- **Quote:** "David reconfirms the special covenant relationship beween the incomparable God (v. 22) and his incomparable people (v. 23)."
- **Locus:** 7:23-24 + EXCURSUS Ransoming and Redeeming; slice L772–797, 829–852 / raw ~4922–4947, 4979–5002
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[2-samuel]], [[davidic-covenant]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R3-32 | 7:25-29 confirm forever; house not temple in prayer keywords; Alter key-word list
- **Claim:** David asks promise of eternal dynasty be confirmed, then eternal blessing on house. “LORD of hosts” = Eternal King enthroned in heaven. Plural “your words are truth” = concrete promises; singular “word” (21, 25) = will/deeds generally. leʿôlām “forever” only here twice in all Samuel (vs ʿad-ʿôlām sixteen times). Alter’s formal motifs in prayer: “speak” (promise/revelation); “house” (dynasty and palace but, in this speech, not temple); “blessing” (three forms in final sentence); “forever” (permanence of promise).
- **Quote:** "“house”: dynasty and palace but, in this speech, not temple;"

### C-R3-33 | Ch. 8 catalogue of victories: geographic not chronological; small empire
- **Claim:** Ch. 8: catalogue of victories (1-14) from Philistines to Transjordan Moab/Ammon through Syrian countries to “the River” Euphrates; ends with administration (15-18). Not necessarily chronological with rest of book. Ammon war chs. 10-12 may be prelude to defeat of Zobah here. V. 13 ties to Ps 60 title. Older empires Egypt/Mesopotamia at low point allowed David advantage. Material possibly earlier period of reign. Organizing principle geography not chronology — four directions: W Philistia / E Moab (1-2); N Aram / S Edom (3-8, 13-14) — small empire Orontes to River of Egypt. David “apparently did not assume” ANE title “the Great King” (melek rab).
- **Quote:** "The organizing principle in this section is not chronology, but geography, since it is “a catalogue of victories”"

### C-R3-34 | 8:1-2 Philistines Metheg-ammah; Moab measuring-cord; vassals
- **Claim:** Defeated Philistines; took Metheg-ammah (unknown; 1 Chr 18:1 “Gath and its villages” — Rainey: Gath-rimmon NW of Gezer). No Philistine battles after David until Hezekiah (2 K 18:8). Moab: measuring-cord selection of POWs (two lots death, one full lot alive) — method not attested elsewhere; Akk. eblu rope-of-land measure. Moab became vassals paying tribute. Earlier fugitive David had left parents with Moab king (1 Sam 22:3); Ruth ancestry noted; now enemies.

### C-R3-35 | Hadadezer of Zobah; possible chronology after chs. 10-12; numbers and horses
- **Claim:** Defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob king of Zobah when he went to restore rule at the River. Subject of belektô = Hadadezer (JPS/REB/NJB), not David; McCarter’s encounter-on-way objection fails — David took initiative to attack. Possible course: Moab (8:2) → Ammon/Aram wars (10) → Rabbah (11-12) → Hadadezer Euphrates attempt and David’s defeat (8:3-14) + Edom. Hadadezer leader of Aramean coalition (10:16); possibly Beth-rehob dynasty; provisional ID with unnamed Aramean in Ashurrabi II annals. Captured 1,700 horsemen + 20,000 foot; hamstrung chariot horses, left 100 — experiment small chariot force; maybe prevent enemy use or Deut 17:16; cavalry useful in mountainous Judah. LXX 1000 chariots + 7000 charioteers; Ap-Thomas 1000/700/20000; pārāšîm may = horse+rider pair.
- **Quote:** "the events of chs. 10-12 may chronologically be the prelude to v. 3."
- **Locus:** 8:3-6; slice L874–944 / raw ~5024–5094
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R3-36 | Aram garrisons; refrain “LORD gave victory”; gold quivers; Toi of Hamath; Edom
- **Claim:** Aram-Damascus helped Hadadezer; David killed 22,000; put garrisons; Aram vassals/tribute. Refrain “the LORD gave David victory wherever he went” ends both sections 1-6 and 7-14 (not premature accident per McCarter). Gold šilṭê = quivers/bow cases (Aram./Akk. šalṭu), not “shields.” Longer versions mention Shoshenq taking them and Solomon using bronze for temple furniture; MT shorter closer to primitive. Betah/Tebah and Berothai (Beqaa). Toi of Hamath sent son Joram/Hadoram with gifts — establish alliance, Israel superior; Yahwistic name as loyalty. Ammon victory listed thematically though war in 11-12. Treasures for temple later. Valley of Salt Edom 18,000; garrisons; all Edom servants. Chronicles ascribes Edom kill to Abishai; Ps 60 title Joab; Hadad escaped (1 K 11).
- **Quote:** "And the LORD gave David victory wherever he went."
- **Locus:** 8:5-14; slice L880–963 / raw ~5030–5113
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R3-37 | David’s officials 8:15-18: justice and righteousness; court posts; Zadok/Abiathar crux; Cherethites; sons as priests
- **Claim:** David ruled all Israel doing justice and righteousness (mišpāṭ ûṣĕdāqāh) for all people — king’s task following Lord who exercises same. List: Joab army general (cf. turtānu); Jehoshaphat recorder (mazkîr) — not necessarily Egyptian wḥmw model (Kitchen/Redford/Mazar reject); Canaanite/Jerusalem city-state admin influence; LB Akkadian tablet fragment outside Old City supports archives. Zadok son of Ahitub + Ahimelech son of Abiathar priests; Seraiah scribe (variants Sheva/Shisha/Shavsha; possibly foreign/Hurrian). Zadok origin debated (Rowley Jebusite Ṣdq cult vs Cross hypocoristicon / Aaronid via Eleazar authentic). Possible MT “Ahimelech son of Abiathar” scribal swap for Abiathar son of Ahimelech, or grandfather-naming + early retirement. Benaiah over Cherethites-Pelethites (Sea Peoples bodyguard). “David’s sons were priests” — duties unknown; not levitical equals of Zadok/Abiathar; Chr “chiefs/officials”; may be royal-family chaplains (cf. Ira 20:26); priestly and royal lines essentially separate.
- **Quote:** "It was the task of the king to establish justice and righteousness (mišpāṭ ûṣĕdāqāh…), following the Lord, who exercises “justice and righteousness”"

### C-R3-39 | Against uniting 9 with 21:1-14 as original sequence
- **Claim:** McCarter (after Klostermann) thinks execution of seven Saulides (21:1-14) originally preceded ch. 9 as a unit with “literary and thematic completeness,” requiring 21:7 (spared Mephibosheth for David–Jonathan oath) as interpolation. Tsumura rejects: if David did not know location/existence of Jonathan’s son — most prominent descendant — he would not have known sons of concubine or daughter; families likely hid after Ishbosheth’s death; Merab’s children still young; Rizpah’s sons much younger.
- **Quote:** "if he did not know the location or even the existence of Jonathan’s son, certainly the most prominent descendant left, how would he have known where the sons of a concubine or a daughter were?"
- **Locus:** EXCURSUS: Relationship of 2 Sam 9 to 21:1-14; slice L1022–1027 / raw ~5172–5177
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[jonathan]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]
- **Misc flag:** Mephibosheth

### C-R3-40 | Literary structure of ch. 9; SETTING ḥesed; Mephibosheth central
- **Claim:** Well-organized unit: SETTING David’s desire to do kindness for Jonathan’s sake (1); Dialogue A king–Ziba (2-5); Dialogue B David–Mephibosheth (6-8); Dialogue A king–Ziba (9-11); TERMINUS Mephibosheth at king’s table (12-13). V. 1 not mere editorial addition — wayyōʾmer + subject often introduces new episode SETTING. Narrator distinguishes second dialogue by “David” not “the king” — central character is Mephibosheth. Threefold *ʿśh + ḥesed (vv. 1, 3, 7) emphasizes motive based on covenant with Jonathan (language reflects 1 Sam 20:14-15; cf. 2:5). V. 3: “kindness of God.”
- **Quote:** "The threefold repetition of the term emphasizes that this is David’s motive."

### C-R3-41 | Ziba, Lo-debar, Machir; Mephibosheth lame; restoration and table
- **Claim:** Ziba servant (ʿebed) of Saul’s house called; identifies Jonathan’s son crippled in both feet (cf. 4:4; 19:26). Located at house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar (N Transjordan; exact site unknown; Machir loyal to Saul’s house, later provisions for David 17:27; name pedigree in N Gilead Manasseh). David brings him; Mephibosheth prostrates. Do not fear: show kindness for Jonathan’s sake; return all land of Saul; eat bread at my table regularly. ʾāb = father Jonathan and grandfather Saul in successive sentences. Dead dog = self-abasement. Gordon: David took kingship but recognized grandson’s right to Saul’s estate (cf. Odyssey I). Table patronage = royal favor (cf. Barzillai sons 1 K 2:7; Jezebel’s prophets; Jehoiachin; Ps 23).
- **Quote:** "Do not be afraid, for I will surely show kindness to you for the sake of Jonathan your father and return to you all the land of Saul your father. As for you, you shall eat bread at my table regularly."
- **Locus:** 9:2-8; slice L1058–1137 / raw ~5208–5287
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[jonathan]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]
- **Misc flag:** Mephibosheth, Ziba, Machir

### C-R3-42 | Ziba as steward; estate arrangement; Mica; inclusio of lameness
- **Claim:** King calls Ziba Saul’s steward (naʿar = estate steward, not “young man” — he had 15 sons and 20 servants). All Saul’s property given to master’s son; Ziba cultivates with sons/servants and brings produce so master’s son has a living; Mephibosheth eats at table. Against McCarter/LXXL emending for dependents only: Rainey — royal courtiers supported by estate income; Mephibosheth eats with David but generally supported by land produce. V. 11b MT “is going to eat at my table like one of the king’s sons” as David’s continued speech (supply “and he said”), not narrator “at David’s table” (LXX). Arrangement like older sons who ate at table but had own houses/fields. Son Mica → multiple descendants (1 Chr 8–9): house of Saul preserved under David’s protection as Jonathan and Saul requested. Inclusio: lame in both feet (v. 3 Ziba; v. 13 narrator) prepares 16:1-4 and 19:24-30.
- **Quote:** "Thus, the house of Saul will be preserved under David’s protection, as requested by Jonathan (1 Sam. 20:14-16) and Saul (24:21-22)."
- **Locus:** 9:9-13; slice L1139–1193 / raw ~5289–5343
- **Targets:** [[david]], [[jonathan]], [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]
- **Misc flag:** Mephibosheth, Ziba, Mica
